_comment: Model capabilities, the FALLBACK for what a node does not report yet (i226 decision 3). The model's weights declare its context ceiling (GGUF <arch>.context_length, HF config max_position_embeddings); the node reports it from the model it serves (heartbeat model_stats[].context_length; Ollama today, noomesh-internal i285) and that report wins. This table caps the window harness placement judges a kind against only where no node reports it: vLLM and llama.cpp placements, and agents older than the report. Each row's `match` globs are tried against the placement's model id, lower-cased, with any registry or org prefix up to the last '/' removed; the first row that matches wins. A model with no row is unknown: no ceiling is assumed, so nothing is refused for it. `max_context` is the model's own context ceiling in tokens; `evidence` says where the number was read. `kv_bytes_per_token` is the cache one token costs per slot, MEASURED on a running daemon; the chat-context memory fit (gateway chat_context.rs, i802) uses it where present instead of placement_fit's conservative fallback.

models.evidence: text_config.max_position_embeddings of google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct and gemma4.context_length of Ollama gemma4:12b, both 262144, read on awolf 2026-10-27

kv_bytes_per_token measured by fa on the default one-box cell (install-matrix run 43622936679, 0.6.24, CPU, num_ctx 16384): container cgroup 5.03 GiB at OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL 4 vs 4.63 GiB at 1, so 0.40 GiB over 3 slots x 16384 tokens = about 8.5 KiB per token per slot (i802). No max_context: the node reports it (131072).
